ideas.pitch: An interactive Python script execution visualizer specifically designed to help Grades 9-12 students step through complex logic puzzles, recursion, and sorting algorithms used in competitive coding.
ideas.title: LogicPython Visualizer for High Schoolers
ideas.why_it_could_win: Since the hackathon is organized by St. Jude's Public School for Grades 9-12 with a strong focus on Python and logical reasoning, a tool that directly helps students master competitive programming logic will resonate heavily with the school judges.

ideas.pitch: A Python-based CLI assistant that takes failing student code snippets in Python, C, C++, or Java, and explains the logical fallacy without giving away the direct solution, fostering true problem-solving skills.
ideas.title: CodeArena AI Coach
ideas.why_it_could_win: Matches the exact stated goal of the event to hone logical reasoning and programming in Python, C, C++, and Java, serving as an educational companion that judges will immediately appreciate for student growth.

ideas.pitch: A lightweight Python benchmarking tool that tests student-submitted Python and C++ functions against edge cases, automatically measuring time and space complexity to prevent Time Limit Exceeded errors.
ideas.title: Algorithmic Complexity Benchmarker
ideas.why_it_could_win: Addresses a pain point familiar to both students and organizers hosting online coding challenges by catching inefficient algorithmic approaches early.

ideas.pitch: A mini multiplayer puzzle platformer controlled purely by writing short Python scripts to solve logic puzzles under a tight 24-hour hackathon timeframe.
ideas.title: Python Logic Duel Arena
ideas.why_it_could_win: Gamifies logical reasoning in Python, fitting the exact skill sets tested during St. Jude's Code Arena while providing an engaging demo for judges.

ideas.pitch: A translator utility that converts basic algorithmic logic written in Python to C, C++, and Java to help high school students transition between the supported contest languages.
ideas.title: Multi-Language Syntax Bridge
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly supports the four official languages of the hackathon (C, C++, Java, Python 3+), making it a practical utility for participants tackling multi-language problem sets.
